title: Integrated RNA-seq and network pharmacology analyses suggest PI3K-Akt and NF-kappaB pathway modulation in the protective effects of diosmin against experimental colitis.
authors: Wang, Shuo; Tan, Cheng; He, Haodong; Li, Xiangyun; Xu, Miao; Guo, Xingzhou; Liu, Yafei; Liao, Fei; Dong, Weiguo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究地奥司明对结肠炎的保护作用，虽含分子对接但核心是转录组和网络药理学，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC), a chronic inflammatory bowel disease, remains difficult to treat due to incomplete understanding of its mechanisms and limited therapeutic options. Diosmin, a natural citrus-derived flavonoid, has shown promising anti-inflammatory effects, but its molecular mechanisms in UC are unclear. In this study, we investigated the protective role of diosmin using dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice and LPS-stimulated HT-29 cells, integrating transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses. Diosmin treatment significantly alleviated colitis symptoms, reduced inflammation, preserved colon length, and enhanced intestinal barrier integrity, with efficacy comparable to 5-aminosalicylic acid. RNA-seq and network pharmacology identified PI3K-Akt and NF-kappaB as key pathways associated with diosmin-mediated protection, while molecular docking was used as a supportive computational analysis to explore potential interactions with selected hub-associated proteins. Experimental validation confirmed that diosmin inhibited activation of PI3K-Akt-mTOR and NF-kappaB signaling, decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and IL-6), increased IL-10, promoted intestinal barrier repair via upregulation of ZO-1, occludin, and E-cadherin, and suppressed apoptosis of colonic epithelial cells. Together, these findings suggest that diosmin exerts multi-target protective effects against experimental colitis by modulating inflammation, supporting barrier integrity, and regulating key signaling pathways, providing mechanistic insight into the actions of this citrus-derived bioactive compound in colitis.
abstract_zh: 溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis, UC）是一种慢性炎症性肠病，由于其机制尚未完全阐明且治疗选择有限，治疗仍具挑战性。地奥司明（diosmin）是一种天然柑橘来源的黄酮类化合物，已显示出良好的抗炎效果，但其在UC中的分子机制尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们利用葡聚糖硫酸钠（dextran sulfate sodium, DSS）诱导的小鼠结肠炎和脂多糖（LPS）刺激的HT-29细胞，结合转录组学和网络药理学分析，探讨了地奥司明的保护作用。地奥司明治疗显著缓解了结肠炎症状，减少了炎症，保持了结肠长度，并增强了肠道屏障完整性，其疗效与5-氨基水杨酸相当。RNA-seq和网络药理学分析确定PI3K-Akt和NF-kappaB为地奥司明介导保护作用的关键通路，同时分子对接（molecular docking）作为辅助计算分析，用于探索与选定核心相关蛋白的潜在相互作用。实验验证证实，地奥司明抑制了PI3K-Akt-mTOR和NF-kappaB信号通路的激活，降低了促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha、IL-1beta和IL-6）水平，增加了IL-10，通过上调ZO-1、occludin和E-cadherin促进肠道屏障修复，并抑制了结肠上皮细胞的凋亡。综上所述，这些发现表明，地奥司明通过调节炎症、支持屏障完整性及调控关键信号通路，对实验性结肠炎发挥多靶点保护作用，为这种柑橘来源生物活性化合物在结肠炎中的作用机制提供了深入见解。
